prompt_text: Who does backflow testing and repair near Liberty MO?
answer_verbatim:
I don’t have live search access from here, so I can’t pull a current list of shops. I can, however, tell you the best ways to find qualified backflow testers and what to ask so you pick a good, compliant provider near Liberty, MO.

How to find testers near Liberty, MO
- Search Google Maps or Yelp for “backflow testing” or “backflow tester” + “Liberty, MO” (or “Kansas City metro”).  
- Check Angi/HomeAdvisor and Nextdoor for locally reviewed contractors.  
- Call the City of Liberty Public Works / Water Department and ask for a list of approved or commonly used backflow testers (many utilities maintain lists or require testers to be on file).  
- Contact local plumbing companies, irrigation/sprinkler companies, and commercial plumbing contractors — many perform backflow testing and repairs.

What to verify before hiring
- Certification: Ask whether the technician is a certified backflow prevention assembly tester (ask for their certification number and the issuing agency).  
- Insurance and plumbing license: Confirm company insurance and any required Missouri plumbing license.  
- Experience with your device type: Make sure they’ve tested/ repaired the same brand/type of assembly (double checkers, reduced pressure, pressure vacuum breakers, etc.).  
- Filing: Ask if they will file the test results with the City of Liberty (or the utility) — many utilities require electronic submission of test reports.  
- Written estimate for repairs: Get a written price for testing and for any repairs/parts before work begins.  
- References/reviews: Check online reviews and ask for references, especially for commercial devices.

Typical cost and turnaround
- Testing alone commonly runs roughly $60–$150 per device (varies). Repairs depend on parts/labor and whether the device must be replaced; get a written estimate.
